skill.name: competitor-profiling
skill.description: Research competitor URLs with Firecrawl and DataForSEO, then produce structured markdown profiles with source references and a cross-competitor summary.
skill.summary: Create source-linked competitor profiles and comparison summaries from supplied URLs.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

security_audit.summary: The static backtick and hardcoded URL findings are false positives caused by markdown examples, placeholder paths, and evaluation prompts. No prompt injection or malicious command execution evidence was found, but the skill intentionally performs external web collection and stores raw competitor data locally.

remediation.issue: External crawling and SEO data collection
remediation.suggestion: Require user-supplied competitor URLs, keep crawl limits narrow, respect site terms and robots guidance, and disclose Firecrawl and DataForSEO use before collecting data.

remediation.issue: Raw scraped data is persisted to disk
remediation.suggestion: Save only data needed for the profile, avoid sensitive personal data, and keep raw files inside the documented project-local competitor-profiles directory.
Document that the skill needs configured external MCP tools and that users should provide explicit collection scope for each run.

semantic_findings.title: External Web Data Collection and Local Persistence
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs Firecrawl and DataForSEO MCP tools to collect competitor website, review, SEO, and backlink data. It also saves raw results under competitor-profiles/raw, so users need explicit scope and careful third-party data handling.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly direct external site mapping, scraping, SEO collection, and saving raw data to disk. The behavior is intentional and legitimate when scoped by the user, but it is a real network and data-retention risk.

content.value_statement: Competitor research is slow when teams gather pages, reviews, and SEO metrics by hand. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create source-linked profiles and comparison summaries from supplied URLs.
actual_capabilities: Maps competitor websites and identifies key pages for research.
Scrapes public pages for positioning, pricing, features, customers, integrations, and changelog signals.
Collects SEO, backlink, keyword, and traffic metrics with DataForSEO MCP tools when available.
Saves raw scrape, review, and SEO data in dated project folders for later review.
Generates structured markdown profiles and a cross-competitor summary document.
Supports quick scans, deep profiles, and update workflows for existing profiles.
limitations: Requires public competitor URLs and configured Firecrawl or DataForSEO MCP tools.
Data quality depends on accessible pages, API coverage, and current public information.
Does not access private, paywalled, or authenticated competitor systems.
Large competitor lists can increase cost, latency, and rate-limit risk.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Competitor Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan for a short competitor list
prompt_templates.prompt: Use competitor-profiling to create quick profiles for these competitor URLs: [URLs]. Focus on homepage, pricing, positioning, and customer proof.

prompt_templates.title: Deep Competitor Profiles
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate research with full public data collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Create deep competitor profiles for [URLs]. Include site scraping, review sources, SEO metrics, backlink signals, strengths, weaknesses, and competitive implications.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Existing Profiles
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced update workflow for stale research
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the existing profiles for [competitors]. Recheck pricing, SEO metrics, changelog activity, and customer proof. Add a change log for each profile.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Competitive Landscape
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced synthesis after individual profiles exist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the completed competitor profiles to create a landscape summary. Compare positioning, pricing, SEO strength, customer proof, opportunities, and threats.

output_examples.input: Profile three SaaS competitors from their public URLs for a positioning review.
output: Creates one markdown profile per competitor with source dates and raw data references.
Summarizes positioning, pricing, product strengths, customer proof, SEO metrics, and competitive implications.
Adds a landscape summary that compares all profiled companies side by side.

output_examples.input: Update an older competitor profile before a quarterly strategy meeting.
output: Rechecks volatile pages such as pricing and changelog pages.
Refreshes SEO and backlink metrics when DataForSEO is available.
Adds a concise change log describing what changed since the last profile.

output_examples.input: Research many competitors but keep the effort controlled.
output: Recommends prioritizing the most relevant competitors first.
Uses quick scan mode for larger lists unless the user requests deep profiles.
Keeps the same metrics across profiles so comparisons remain fair.

best_practices: Provide your own product context before asking for competitor comparisons.
Use quick scans for large lists and deep profiles for the highest-priority competitors.
Review raw source files before using findings in public sales or marketing material.
anti_patterns: Do not profile private systems, authenticated pages, or non-public competitor data.
Do not treat customer logo walls as complete proof without cross-checking other sources.
Do not compare competitors using different metrics or different collection dates.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs competitor URLs, your product context, desired depth, and any focus areas such as pricing or SEO.

faq.question: Does it use live web data?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to use Firecrawl and DataForSEO MCP tools when those tools are configured.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It creates markdown competitor profiles, a summary file, and dated raw data folders for scrapes, reviews, and SEO responses.

faq.question: Can it handle many competitors at once?
faq.answer: Yes, but it recommends quick scans and prioritization when the list is large.

faq.question: Can it skip SEO data?
faq.answer: Yes. The user can request a scoped profile that skips DataForSEO and focuses on pages such as pricing and customers.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for legal or compliance review?
faq.answer: No. Users should confirm crawling scope, terms, data handling, and publication rules for their own use case.
